candidates.name: Existing UAR observers, host admission, approvals and team catalog

evidence.claim: Durable subscription/inbox recovery and bounded occurrence delivery already exist.
Catalog claim/reclaim preserves epochs, queued transfers and uncertain running work.

risks: Observer polling is not a user recurrence contract.
Existing owner identity includes tenant/subject but needs issuer policy reconciliation.
Kernel execution remains behind trusted host admission.
candidates.decision_rationale: Extend current contracts with stable scheduled occurrences and a delivery outbox; avoid a second authority or task-state system.

candidates.name: tokio-cron-scheduler 0.15.1

evidence.claim: Tagged README documents cron, one-shot/repeated jobs, timezone APIs and optional Postgres/Nats stores.
Context7 documents timezone-aware JobBuilder; main-branch snippets are not pinned API certification.
Registry reports stable 0.15.1, released 2025-10-28, and dual MIT/Apache licensing.

risks: Adoption is conditional on exact-version DST/missed-run/restart tests; no such tests run in Analyze.
Durable UAR records must remain authoritative; callbacks may request admission, never execute tools directly.
It adds a scheduler dependency; if its timing adapter duplicates UAR scanning without reducing recurrence complexity, reject it at the planned fit gate.
candidates.decision_rationale: Preferred candidate for wrapping timing functionality only. Do not adopt its persistence as a second source of truth. No dependency introduced or final pin authorized by this artifact.

candidates.name: Apalis 0.7.4 stable / 1.0.0-rc.12 prerelease
candidates.fit_for_gap: R6 ingestion and D1 durable job dispatch

evidence.claim: Stable README lists persistent SQL/Redis jobs and cron piping into backends.
Current indexed docs list multiple backends; those main-branch APIs are not assumed compatible with stable 0.7.4.

risks: No SurrealDB backend established in inspected docs.
No evidence that stock queues atomically commit with UAR document metadata or enforce host receipt uncertainty.
Stable and prerelease APIs differ; do not mix examples.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use queue/backoff ideas as a shared-host reference. Local operation and shared hosting are equally required in the first release; any adoption must preserve both profiles and coherent UAR outbox semantics. Adding a second job store is not justified by that requirement alone.

candidates.name: Temporal Rust SDK 1.1.0
candidates.fit_for_gap: D1 scheduling and R5/R9 durable orchestration

maintenance.license_review: Registry returned non-standard; exact license not resolved in this bounded pass.

evidence.claim: Current README describes connected workers, workflow replay constraints and activities. It no longer contains the preview label returned by the docs index.
Context7 preview snippet conflicts with the current primary document; preview status is not accepted as current evidence.

risks: Separate server and workflow execution model add operational and migration scope.
UAR authority, tenant isolation, approvals and unknown effects still need domain integration.
Current main docs are not exact-tag API certification; licensing remains unresolved.
candidates.decision_rationale: Keep as a shared-host orchestration comparison, not the default phase dependency. Both local operation and shared hosting are equally required from the first release; adoption would need to preserve local operation and coherent UAR authority/state. Do not reject on the stale preview claim.

candidates.name: Existing UAR MemoryService and vendored surreal-memory 0.1.0

evidence.claim: Memory is a path dependency under vendor/git/surreal-memory-server; Cargo.lock reports 0.1.0 without registry source.
Service exposes retrieval/capture/mutation helpers but user scoping passes subject IDs without the complete tenant/issuer identity.

risks: Vendor tree is committed source, not the historical revision named in versions.toml.
Every memory surface, including native/MCP, legacy HTTP and embedded SDK, needs current owner enforcement.
Workflow mirror persistence is not assistant memory privacy certification.
candidates.decision_rationale: Preserve the existing memory engine and extend host scoping, consent, deletion and source provenance. A new memory database would not repair the identity boundary.

candidates.name: Existing UAR persistence adapters with transactional outbox and settlement records

evidence.claim: Existing persistence boundary includes durable capabilities and also checkpoint/cost defaults requiring explicit unsupported behavior.
Postgres cost recording currently appends scope/amount rows without a run/call settlement key.

risks: Atomicity must be implemented and tested per supported backend, not assumed from a trait.
Source-blob/outbox coordination requires a durable content-reference protocol if bytes are not in the same transaction.
Shared-host consistency and single-device restart must be separately proven.
candidates.decision_rationale: Keep data and admission state in current stores. Build narrow domain transactions and uniqueness/CAS contracts rather than introduce a generic job framework as a correctness substitute.

candidates.name: Pinned Liter 2.1.1 SSE parser and UAR provider boundary
candidates.fit_for_gap: R4 streaming framing and terminal truth

evidence.claim: Checked-out parser buffers UTF-8/lines and rejects incomplete buffered EOF, but empty-buffer EOF returns no error without a terminal sentinel.
UAR requires terminal completion conditionally; the native Anthropic parser is a separate route.

risks: Do not replace provider-specific message/event parsing with a generic data-line parser without compatibility checks.
No wire-level reproduction or complete provider matrix ran.
versions.toml policy pins still require an explicit reconciliation change.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reuse proven framing ideas from exact checked-out source while enforcing protocol completion at the host provider boundary. A library upgrade alone does not resolve UAR's conditional success.
